items.title: For a smooth equidimensional scheme over a base of dimension one the bivariant Chow ring is Chow homology and composition becomes intersection
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)

items.difficulty_reason: With (S, delta) as in the section and X smooth and equidimensional of dimension d over S, the lemma asserts that c -> c cap [X]_d is an isomorphism A^p(X) -> CH_{d-p}(X) turning composition of bivariant classes into the intersection product (statement lines 14978-14988). As in the field case the map factors through a bivariant group, now as A^p(X) -> A^{p-d+1}(X -> S) -> CH_{d-p}(X): the first arrow is c -> c o g^* from Proposition labelled proposition-compute-bivariant and the second is c -> c cap [S]_1 from Lemma labelled lemma-chow-cohomology-towards-base-dim-1 (proof lines 14990-14996). The proof then reads the inverses off the two cited proofs: the inverse of the second arrow sends alpha to the class acting by beta -> alpha x beta and the inverse of the first sends it to the class acting by beta -> Delta^!(alpha x beta) = alpha . beta, which is the statement about composition (proof lines 14998-15010). Chasing the two explicit inverses in the dimension one theory is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
